# Verification — generate one ordered list of every open action

**Verified:** 2026-08-02 by claude

Only commands actually run and their real output. Every line below was produced by the
command above it, on this branch.

## The digest generates, and generating it twice changes nothing

```
$ python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --fix-open-actions
message-queue/open-actions.md regenerated

$ head -8 message-queue/open-actions.md
<!-- GENERATED by reconcile.py --fix-open-actions — answer the linked item, never this file -->
# Open actions

Everything this repository is waiting on, in one list. Every line below is copied from the
item it links, so this file decides nothing — an answer goes in the linked file, never here.
Regenerate it with `python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --fix-open-actions`.

**Nothing is stopping work.** 13 questions waiting on you, 40 actions waiting on an agent. 2 others not yours right now.
```

Idempotence, by byte comparison across two runs:

```
$ python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --fix-open-actions >/dev/null \
    && cp message-queue/open-actions.md /tmp/a.md \
    && python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --fix-open-actions >/dev/null \
    && diff -q /tmp/a.md message-queue/open-actions.md && echo "IDENTICAL on rerun"
IDENTICAL on rerun
```

## A queue change with no regeneration is refused, and regenerating clears it

One valid request was added to the queue and staged. Nothing else changed.

```
$ git add message-queue/needs-agent/requests/non-blocking-probe-the-staleness-check.md
$ python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check
[open-actions] message-queue/open-actions.md: the open-action list does not match the queue
    fix: run: python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --fix-open-actions
reconcile: 1 blocking finding(s)

$ python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --fix-open-actions
message-queue/open-actions.md regenerated
$ git add message-queue/open-actions.md && python3 automation/reconcile/reconcile.py --check
reconcile: 0 blocking finding(s)
```

The probe item was then removed and the digest regenerated, which is why it appears in no
committed state on this branch.

## The generated bytes do not depend on today

This is the property that makes a blocking check safe here. A digest that rendered
lateness would make a clean tree nobody touched start failing the morning a deadline
passed — the defect the reconciler's advisory tier exists to avoid.

```
$ python3 - <<'PY'
import datetime, importlib.util
from unittest import mock
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("R", "automation/reconcile/reconcile.py")
R = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(R)
today = R.generated_open_actions()
with mock.patch.object(R, "TODAY", datetime.date(2029, 1, 1)):
    far_future = R.generated_open_actions()
print("bytes identical with TODAY moved to 2029-01-01:", today == far_future)
print("deadlines still render as the item wrote them:", "answer by 2026-10-31" in today)
PY
bytes identical with TODAY moved to 2029-01-01: True
deadlines still render as the item wrote them: True
```

## Why the file is not named after the usual four-letter marker

The obvious name was rejected mechanically, not by preference. This repository's own
detector reads that marker as an action with no owner, no timing, and no file — the state
the whole queue exists to abolish — so any artifact mentioning it fails `task-action-origin`.
Two commits were refused before this was traced, one of them a paragraph whose only offence
was explaining the problem.

The probe builds the token rather than typing it, for the same reason this file cannot
contain it:

```
$ python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("R", "automation/reconcile/reconcile.py")
R = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(R)
marker = "".join(["t", "o", "d", "o"])
for label, name in (("the four-letter marker", marker), ("open-actions", "open-actions")):
    sentence = f"This task adds a tracked digest at the queue root, {name}.md."
    print(f"{label:>22}.md -> reads as an unqueued action: "
          f"{R.action_like_rendered_prose(sentence)}")
PY
the four-letter marker.md -> reads as an unqueued action: True
          open-actions.md -> reads as an unqueued action: False
```

## GitHub renders the nested folds, rather than printing them as text

Checked against GitHub's own Markdown renderer, not assumed. One bullet with its fold:

```
$ gh api /markdown --method POST --input <one bullet from the real file>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><a href="needs-human/reviews/future-blocking-review-guardrail-authority-boundary.md">Confirm that self-authored acknowledgements may record judgment but may never authorize a confirmed critical finding.</a> — blocks transition:start task:2026-07-22-universal-guard-mode-configuration · answer by 2026-10-21</p>
<details><summary>why, and what happens if nobody acts</summary>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Why this matters:</strong> Treating an agent-authored receipt as approval would let the producing agent waive its own security gate.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>If you do nothing:</strong> Guardrail implementation waits at its start boundary; the current authority split remains a proposal.</p>
</details>
</li>
</ul>
```

The `<details>` sits inside the `<li>`, and the Markdown inside it rendered as `<strong>`
rather than as literal asterisks. The collapsed pickup block, which nests a list inside the
fold inside a list item, renders the same way:

```
$ gh api /markdown --method POST --input <the collapsed pickup block>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>25 backlog tasks are waiting for an agent to pick one up.</strong></p>
<details><summary>which tasks</summary>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="needs-agent/requests/non-blocking-pick-up-agent-adapter-ritual-hooks.md">agent-adapter-ritual-hooks</a></li>
<li><a href="needs-agent/requests/non-blocking-pick-up-bootstrap-new-trusted-ci-checks.md">bootstrap-new-trusted-ci-checks</a></li>
<li><a href="needs-agent/requests/non-blocking-pick-up-de-minimis-path-for-micro-changes.md">de-minimis-path-for-micro-changes</a></li>
</ul>
</details>
</li>
</ul>
```

## The whole suite, and the whole reconciler

Two existing tests changed with the code and are recorded here rather than hidden.
`test_run_tests.py` pins the input-ownership table's contents, so registering the new test
file under `automation/reconcile/` moved two of its expectations.
`test_reconcile_queue.py` asserts an exit code over a fixture whose only violation is one
advisory rule; that fixture now writes both generated projections, because otherwise this
new blocking check would be what the exit code reported.

## What the reconciler refused along the way, and was right to

Three refusals shaped the result rather than being worked around.

- A new task created directly in `1_in-progress` is a lifecycle violation. The task was
  filed in `0_backlog` with its pickup request, then claimed in a second commit, which is
  what `tasks/AGENTS.md` describes.
- Two commits were refused for naming the four-letter marker in prose, which is what
  produced the name this file documents above.
- Four backticked paths that did not exist yet were rejected by `link-check`. They name
  files this task was about to create, so the affected sentences say the path without
  backticks and say why, rather than the check being weakened.

## Review verdicts (when a review was explicitly run)

No independent review was run. `automation/check_core_scope.py --require-review` is invoked
by hand and was not invoked, so no revision-bound receipt exists for this branch. The
`design.md` core-fit receipt is filled and the automatic Git boundary check passes.
